articles.title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
articles.summary: In accordance with subsection (e)(12) of the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), is providing notice of a computer matching program between CMS and the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The purpose of the matching program is to identify beneficiaries enrolled in both Medicare and VHA health care and to identify medical claims for which both agencies made payment for the same health care services. Under this agreement, the VHA will provide CMS with a finder file on a recurring basis, of all Veteran beneficiaries enrolled in VHA health care that CMS will use to identify dually enrolled beneficiaries. CMS and VHA will use the results of the matching program to recover duplicate payments, improve payment accuracy, and identify potential fraud, waste, and abuse.

articles.title: Authorization of Emergency Use for Four Animal Drugs for the Prevention and Treatment of New World Screwworm; Availability
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or the Agency) is announcing the issuance of four Emergency Use Authorizations (EUA or Authorization) under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) for new animal products. FDA has issued one EUA for an animal product as requested by Elanco US Inc. for application on or around wounds for the prevention of infestations caused by New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax; NWS) larvae (myiasis) in sheep, cattle, goats, swine, camelids, and the following captive and captured wildlife species: cervids, American bison, bighorn sheep, and Sonoran pronghorn. FDA has issued one EUA for an animal product as requested by Zoetis Inc. for the treatment of infestations caused by NWS (myiasis) in dogs and puppies. FDA has issued one EUA for an animal product as requested by Bimeda Animal Health Ltd. for the prevention of infestations caused by NWS (myiasis) in cattle. FDA has issued one EUA for an animal product as requested by Sergeant's Pet Care Products LLC for the treatment and prevention of infestations caused by NWS (myiasis) in dogs, puppies, cats and kittens 2 pounds of body weight or greater and 4 weeks of age and older. The Authorizations contain, among other things, conditions on the emergency use of the authorized products. The Authorizations follow the August 18, 2025, determination by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) that there is a significant potential for a public health emergency that has a significant potential to affect national security or the health and security of U.S. citizens living abroad and that involves NWS. On the basis of such determination, the Secretary of HHS declared on August 18, 2025, that circumstances exist justifying the authorization of emergency use of animal drugs to treat or prevent NWS myiasis in animals. The Authorizations, which include an explanation of the reasons for issuance, are reprinted in this document.

articles.title: Use of Salt Substitutes To Reduce the Sodium Content in Standardized Foods
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is issuing a final rule to amend our standard of identity regulations that specify salt (sodium chloride) as a required or optional ingredient to permit the use of salt substitutes in standardized foods, to reduce the sodium content. Reducing sodium may help reduce the risk of hypertension, a major risk factor for heart disease and stroke. The rule will help support a healthier food supply by providing flexibility to facilitate industry innovation in the production of standardized foods lower in sodium while maintaining the basic nature and essential characteristics of the foods.

articles.title: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA); Virtual Access, Gynecologic Cytology Proficiency Testing (PT), Personnel Qualifications, and Other Changes
articles.summary: This proposed rule would amend the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA) regulations to allow for virtual access under the CLIA certificate of the primary testing laboratory that generated the data, with the exception of the subspecialty of cytology, and the use of digital images for gynecologic cytology proficiency testing. This proposed rule also includes proposed changes to personnel qualification requirements and other proposed changes pertaining to SARS-CoV-2 reporting requirements, certificate requirements, test reporting requirements, enforcement requirements, public consultation requirements, and editorial and technical updates. These proposed updates aim to strengthen the Federal oversight of clinical laboratories and ensure accurate and reliable patient test results while adapting to modern technological capabilities and industry needs, including workforce shortages.

articles.summary: On May 28, 2010, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) issued Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) guidance related to the "generic" clearance process. Generally, this is an expedited process by which agencies may obtain OMB's approval of collection of information requests that are "usually voluntary, low- burden, and uncontroversial collections," do not raise any substantive or policy issues, and do not require policy or methodological review. The process requires the submission of an overarching plan that defines the scope of the individual collections that would fall under its umbrella. On October 23, 2011, OMB approved our initial request to use the generic clearance process under control number 0938-1148 (CMS- 10398). It was last approved on April 26, 2021, via the standard PRA process which included the publication of 60- and 30-day Federal Register notices. The scope of the April 2021 umbrella accounts for Medicaid and CHIP State plan amendments, waivers, demonstrations, and reporting. This Federal Register notice seeks public comment on one or more of our collection of information requests that we believe are generic and fall within the scope of the umbrella. Interested persons are invited to submit comments regarding our burden estimates or any other aspect of this collection of information, including: the necessity and utility of the proposed information collection for the proper performance of the agency's functions, the accuracy of the estimated burden, ways to enhance the quality, utility and clarity of the information to be collected, and the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology to minimize the information collection burden.

The nurses, who are members of Maine State Nurses Association/National Nurses Organizing Committee, had sent a petition of no confidence in Zewe to the board of trustees in July 2026.

articles.title: Union election at MedStar Franklin Square too close to call and marred by MedStar Health union busting

The results were inconclusive at the end of the night, with challenged ballots still to be resolved.

articles.title: UMC New Orleans nurses to hold press conference on LCMC short-changing patients and nurses
articles.summary: In the wake of LCMC’s “Spirit of Charity Gala” last week, Registered Nurses from University Medical Center (UMC) in New Orleans, La., will hold a press conference on Friday, Oct. 16, to highlight their patient safety concerns, including short-staffing, high turnover, and wage theft.

articles.title: National Nurses United endorses Rep. Ramirez’s Reimagining Safety Act
articles.summary: National Nurses United (NNU), the largest union of registered nurses in the United States with more than 225,000 members, is proud to endorse Representative Delia Ramirez’s Reimagining Safety Act to abolish ICE, reinvest in care.

articles.title: Wichita nurses ratify new contract with strong measures to improve patient safety and nurse retention
articles.summary: Registered nurses at Ascension Via Christi St. Francis and St. Joseph hospitals in Wichita, Kansas, voted overwhelmingly in favor of ratifying a new three-year contract today, winning protections to improve patient safety and nurse retention.

articles.title: When Home is Not Safe
articles.summary: Since the Trump administration began targeting immigrants and Black and brown people for deportation, nurses have long been concerned about how these actions hurt patients — whether it’s federal agents using excessive force on people they are trying to detain or even killing them, showing up at hospitals with detainees needing medical attention and putting the entire facility in a panic, or instilling so much fear in our communities that people just stop seeking medical care because they can’t go outside.

articles.title: Open House
articles.summary: Education and information is vital to an effective Professional Practice Committee (PPC), an essential committee elected by the nurses and representing each major nursing unit in the facility. The PPC usually meets monthly on paid time and is an essential part of contracts negotiations. The PPC has the authority to document unsafe practices and the power to meet with management and make real changes across the facility.

articles.title: Ambassador details how U.S. fuel blockade harms Cuban health
articles.summary: On July 10, Cuban ambassador to the United States, Dr. Tanieris Diéguez, and other embassy officials visited with National Nurses United RN members and allied political and community groups to describe first hand the devastation the current United States fuel blockade of Cuba was unnecessarily wreaking upon the daily lives and public health of the Cuban people.

articles.title: HCA Swedish nurses unionize
articles.summary: The second election comes after the National Labor Relations Board ruled that the employer, HCA Healthcare, the country’s largest hospital system, illegally interfered with a previous union election held in 2024. That now-invalidated 2024 election was marred by illegal interference by the employer.

articles.title: Santa Ana nurses ratify first contract
articles.summary: Registered nurses at Orange County Global Medical Center in Santa Ana, Calif. voted overwhelmingly on Sept. 10, 2026 to ratify their inclusion into the existing union contract covering KPC Health registered nurses represented by California Nurses Association. This first contract for Orange County Global nurses secures them important new protections to improve patient safety and nurse retention.

articles.title: New report finds cost-cutting at MedStar Franklin Square puts patient care in jeopardy
articles.summary: A new report, “The Cost of Cutting Care: How MedStar Is Failing Franklin Square Nurses and Patients”, released by National Nurses United, finds chronic registered nurse (RN) understaffing by MedStar Franklin Square Medical Center in Baltimore, Md., puts patient care at risk and leads to numerous poor outcomes as measured by U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

articles.title: 35,000 nurses in Northern and Central California head into bargaining
articles.summary: Registered nurses from the Kaiser Permanente and Sutter Health systems held a joint protest on Sept. 16 to rally for strong contracts to improve patient care at two of the Bay’s biggest hospital systems.

articles.title: Nurses put D.C. hospitals on RED ALERT
articles.summary: Registered nurses will hold a rally and community event on Saturday, Oct. 10 in Washington, D.C. to demand that MedStar Washington Hospital Center reopen its shuttered postpartum unit in the midst of a Black maternal health crisis in the District. Following the rally, the nurses and allies in the community will make their way to the hospital where they will deliver a letter to management calling for the immediate reopening of the unit.

articles.title: RNs fight back with strike against anti-union employer
articles.summary: Michigan Nurses Association RNs at MyMichigan Medical Center Alma held a three-day unfair labor practice strike over the July 4 weekend to protest the employer’s unfair labor practices and advocate for a fair contract.

articles.title: Landmark nurse-sponsored bills regulating A.I. pass Legislature
articles.summary: Union nurses with California Nurses Association (CNA) celebrated the final passage through both houses of the California Legislature of two CNA-sponsored bills with landmark guardrails on the use of artificial intelligence (A.I.) in health care, now awaiting Gov. Gavin Newsom's signature.

articles.title: Prime Healthcare nurses stage national uprising
articles.summary: Nurses at Prime Healthcare facilities across the country are fired up and fed up with chronic short staffing, lack of supplies and working equipment at their hospitals, and being forced to do more with less at every turn. This is why they are unionizing, picketing, and striking from California to Maine, speaking up for their patients, their communities, and themselves.

articles.title: Nurses demand Palantir out!
articles.summary: On Aug. 27, National Nurses United in eight cities across the country held civil disobedience protests by briefly stopping traffic to demand that their hospital systems, government and elected officials, and other institutions immediately cut ties with the A.I. tech company Palantir.
